question: How do I get my criminal record sealed or expunged, how long do I have to wait, and what does it cost?

groups: elapsed from the date of arrest

gold_sections.why: Precondition (not itself a ground) for the no-charge, dismissal and limitations grounds of 55A.052-55A.054: released, no final conviction and nothing pending, and no court-ordered community supervision (other than for a Class C misdemeanor).

No charge presented: the waiting periods from arrest (180 days Class C, one year Class A/B, three years felony or where a felony charge arose from the same transaction) or a prosecutor's certification.
A charge that was filed and dismissed or quashed qualifies only for a listed reason (veterans, mental health or pretrial intervention program completion, no probable cause, void charge).
Expunction once the limitations period has expired (the usual route for a charge dismissed for any other reason).
Entitlement to expunction after acquittal by the trial court.
Where to file: an ex parte petition in a district court for the county of arrest or of the alleged offense.
Hearing set no earlier than 30 days after filing; notice to every listed agency; $25 per agency that cannot receive electronic notice.
Who decides: the court must order expunction if it finds the petitioner entitled.
Cost: the civil ex parte filing fee in district court, $100 in a justice or municipal court of record; waivers (acquittal petitions within 30 days, veterans and mental health court) and refund.

Nondisclosure after deferred adjudication: petition the court that placed the person on deferred adjudication; waiting periods (at discharge, second anniversary, fifth anniversary); best-interest standard.

Conditions for every nondisclosure order: no new non-traffic offense during supervision or the waiting period; excluded offenses (sex-offender registration, murder, trafficking, stalking, family violence and others).
How to petition for nondisclosure (in person, electronically or by mail), the civil filing fee, notice to the state, and when a hearing is required (state's 45 days).
Automatic nondisclosure for first-time deferred adjudication on most misdemeanors: the court must issue the order on discharge (180-day rule) for a $28 fee.
Nondisclosure of certain misdemeanor convictions after the sentence is completed (immediately for fine-only, otherwise after two years); violent or sexual offenses excluded.
State consolidated civil fee: $137 on filing any civil case in a district, statutory county or county court (part of the civil filing fee for expunction and nondisclosure petitions).
Local consolidated civil fee: $213 on filing any civil case in a district, statutory county or county court, in addition to all other fees and court costs.
No expunction of an acquittal when another offense in the same criminal episode resulted in conviction or is still prosecutable.
After a trial acquittal the court must enter the expunction order within 30 days on request and must tell the person of the right.
Fine-only offenses: the petition may be filed in a justice court or municipal court of record.
Petition must be verified and list the person's identifying details, the arrest, and every agency or entity with records.
The person or a protesting agency may appeal the decision as in other civil cases.
Clerk sends the final order to DPS, the Office of Court Administration and each listed agency.
DPS notifies federal depositories and private background-check entities.
Listed agencies return or obliterate the records and delete index references.
Effect of expunction: records may not be used for any purpose and the person may deny the arrest.

Nondisclosure after community supervision (probation) following a misdemeanor conviction: first offenders only; at completion for most misdemeanors, second anniversary for Penal Code chapters 20, 21, 22, 25, 42, 43, 46.

DWI or BWI deferred adjudication (excluded from 411.0725): first offenders only, petition on or after the second anniversary of completion and discharge; denied if the offense caused a collision involving another person.
After a nondisclosure order: clerk to DPS within 15 business days, DPS seals within 10 business days and forwards, agencies seal within 30 business days.
Effect of nondisclosure: no duty to disclose the proceeding on job, information or licensing applications.
What counts as deferred adjudication for nondisclosure purposes.

nuggets.text: A person who was tried and acquitted by the trial court is entitled to have the arrest records expunged, unless the person was convicted of, or is still prosecutable for, another offense in the same criminal episode (Article 55A.151).
nuggets.quote: acquitted by the trial court, except as provided by Article 55A.151

nuggets.text: The no-charge, dismissal and limitations grounds for expunction (Subchapter B) apply only to a person who was released, whose charge did not result in a final conviction and is no longer pending, and who had no court-ordered community supervision (probation or deferred adjudication) for the offense other than for a Class C misdemeanor; meeting these conditions is necessary but not enough, since one of the grounds in 55A.052-55A.054 must also be met.
nuggets.quote: the person has been released; (2) the charge, if any, has not resulted in a final conviction and is no longer pending; and (3) there was no court-ordered community supervision under Chapter 42A for the offense, other than for a Class C misdemeanor

nuggets.text: If no indictment or information was ever presented, the person is entitled to expunction once at least 180 days have passed since the arrest for a Class C misdemeanor or one year for a Class A or B misdemeanor (in both cases only if no felony charge arose from the same transaction), or three years for a felony or where a felony charge arose from the same transaction; or at any time if the prosecutor certifies the records are not needed for any investigation or prosecution.
nuggets.quote: at least 180 days have elapsed from the date of arrest if the arrest for which the expunction was sought was for an offense punishable as a Class C misdemeanor and there was no felony charge arising out of the same transaction for which the person was arrested; (2) at least one year has elapsed from the date of arrest if the arrest for which the expunction was sought was for an offense punishable as a Class B or A misdemeanor and there was no felony charge arising out of the same transaction for which the person was arrested; (3) at least three years have elapsed from the date of arrest if the arrest for which the expunction was sought was for an offense punishable as a felony or there was a felony charge arising out of the same transaction for which the person was arrested; or (4) the attorney representing the state certifies that the applicable arrest records and files are not needed for use in any criminal investigation or prosecution

nuggets.text: If a charge was filed and then dismissed or quashed, the person is entitled to expunction only if the court finds it was dismissed because the person completed a veterans treatment court, mental health court or pretrial intervention program, because of mistake or false information showing no probable cause, or because the charge was void.
nuggets.quote: the court finds that the indictment or information was dismissed or quashed because: (A) the person completed a veterans treatment court program created under Chapter 124, Government Code, or former law, subject to Subsection (b); (B) the person completed a mental health court program created under Chapter 125, Government Code, or former law, subject to Subsection (c); (C) the person completed a pretrial intervention program authorized under Section 76.011, Government Code, other than a program described by Paragraph (A) or (B); (D) the presentment of the indictment or information was made because of mistake, false information, or other similar reason indicating absence of probable cause at the time of the dismissal to believe the person committed the offense; or (E) the indictment or information was void

nuggets.text: A person who meets the 55A.051 conditions is also entitled to expunction once prosecution is no longer possible because the limitations period has expired (the usual route when a charge was dismissed for some other reason).
nuggets.quote: is entitled to have all records and files relating to the arrest expunged if prosecution of the person for the offense for which the person was arrested is no longer possible because the limitations period has expired

nuggets.text: An eligible person files an ex parte petition for expunction in a district court for the county where the person was arrested or where the offense allegedly occurred.
nuggets.quote: file an ex parte petition for expunction in a district court for the county in which: (1) the petitioner was arrested; or (2) the offense was alleged to have occurred

nuggets.text: Expunction filing fee: in district court, the ordinary fee for filing an ex parte petition in a civil action; in a justice court or municipal court of record (available for fine-only offenses, 55A.252), $100; in both cases in addition to any other fees required by law, and subject to the waivers in subsections (c) and (d).
nuggets.quote: In addition to any other fees required by other law and except as provided by Subsections (c) and (d), a petitioner seeking expunction of a criminal record in a district court shall pay the fee charged for filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court. (b) In addition to any other fees required by other law and except as provided by Subsection (c), a petitioner seeking expunction of a criminal record in a justice court or a municipal court of record under Chapter 55A shall pay a fee of $100 for filing an ex parte petition for expunction

nuggets.text: The clerk of a district, statutory county or county court collects a $137 state consolidated fee on filing any civil case (part of the base civil filing fee for an expunction or nondisclosure petition).
nuggets.quote: The clerk of a district court, statutory county court, statutory probate court, or county court shall collect: (1) a fee in the amount of $137 on the filing of any civil, probate, guardianship, or mental health case

nuggets.text: A $213 local consolidated filing fee is paid on filing any civil case in a district, statutory county or county court, in addition to all other fees and court costs (with the $137 state fee, a base of $350 before any county-specific fees).
nuggets.quote: A person shall pay in a district court, statutory county court, or county court in addition to all other fees and court costs a local consolidated filing fee of: (1) $213 on filing any civil case except a probate, guardianship, or mental health case

nuggets.text: After a discharge and dismissal of deferred adjudication (other than DWI or BWI, and where the automatic order of 411.072 is not available), the person may petition the court that placed them on deferred adjudication for an order of nondisclosure: at the discharge and dismissal for most misdemeanors, on or after its second anniversary for misdemeanors under Penal Code chapters 20, 21, 22, 25, 42, 43 or 46, and on or after its fifth anniversary for a felony.
nuggets.quote: A person may petition the court that placed the person on deferred adjudication community supervision for an order of nondisclosure of criminal history record information under this section only on or after: (1) the discharge and dismissal, if the offense for which the person was placed on deferred adjudication was a misdemeanor other than a misdemeanor described by Subdivision (2); (2) the second anniversary of the discharge and dismissal, if the offense for which the person was placed on deferred adjudication was a misdemeanor under Chapter 20, 21, 22, 25, 42, 43, or 46, Penal Code; or (3) the fifth anniversary of the discharge and dismissal, if the offense for which the person was placed on deferred adjudication was a felony

nuggets.text: Every order of nondisclosure requires that, during the sentence or community supervision and during any waiting period afterward, the person was not convicted of or placed on deferred adjudication for any offense other than a fine-only traffic offense.
nuggets.quote: during the period after the court pronounced the sentence or placed the person on community supervision, including deferred adjudication community supervision, for the offense for which the order of nondisclosure is requested, and during any applicable waiting period for the person under this subchapter following completion of the person's sentence or community supervision, including deferred adjudication community supervision, the person is not convicted of or placed on deferred adjudication community supervision for any offense other than a traffic offense that is punishable by fine only

nuggets.text: No order of nondisclosure is available if the offense, or any earlier conviction or deferred adjudication, is for an offense requiring sex-offender registration, aggravated kidnapping (Penal Code 20.04), murder or capital murder (19.02, 19.03), trafficking (20A.02, 20A.03), injury to a child, elderly or disabled person (22.04), child abandonment or endangerment (22.041), violation of protective orders or bond conditions (25.07, 25.072), stalking (42.072), or any other family violence offense, or if the court finds the offense involved family violence.
nuggets.quote: the person requests the order of nondisclosure for, or the person has been previously convicted of or placed on deferred adjudication community supervision for: (A) an offense requiring registration as a sex offender under Chapter 62, Code of Criminal Procedure; (B) an offense under Section 20.04, Penal Code, regardless of whether the offense is a reportable conviction or adjudication for purposes of Chapter 62, Code of Criminal Procedure; (C) an offense under Section 19.02, 19.03, 20A.02, 20A.03, 22.04, 22.041, 25.07, 25.072, or 42.072, Penal Code; or (D) any other offense involving family violence, as defined by Section 71.004, Family Code; or (2) the court makes an affirmative finding that the offense for which the order of nondisclosure is requested involved family violence

nuggets.text: A nondisclosure petition must be accompanied by the fee that generally applies to filing a civil case.
nuggets.quote: The petition must be accompanied by payment of a fee that generally applies to the filing of a civil case.

nuggets.text: For a first-time deferred adjudication on a misdemeanor outside the excluded categories (DWI or BWI, Penal Code chapters 20, 21, 22, 25, 42, 43, 46 or 71, or a family-violence finding), the court itself must issue the order of nondisclosure at the discharge and dismissal if it comes 180 days or more after the deferral, otherwise as soon as practicable after the 180th day; the person presents evidence of eligibility and pays a $28 fee to the clerk.
nuggets.quote: at the time the court discharges and dismisses the proceedings against the person, if the discharge and dismissal occurs on or after the 180th day after the date the court placed the person on deferred adjudication community supervision; or (2) as soon as practicable on or after the 180th day after the date the court placed the person on deferred adjudication community supervision, if the discharge and dismissal occurred before that date. (c) The person shall present to the court any evidence necessary to establish that the person is eligible to receive an order of nondisclosure of criminal history record information under this section. The person must pay a $28 fee to the clerk of the court before the court issues the order.

nuggets.text: A first offender (no prior conviction or deferred adjudication other than fine-only traffic) convicted of a misdemeanor other than an intoxication offense under Penal Code 49.04, 49.05, 49.06 or 49.065, Alcoholic Beverage Code 106.041 (minor driving under the influence) or Penal Code chapter 71 (organized crime), who completed the sentence, may petition the court that imposed the sentence for nondisclosure: on completion for a fine-only misdemeanor, otherwise on or after the second anniversary of completing the sentence; the court may not grant it for a violent or sexual offense other than assault under Penal Code 22.01 (probation after a misdemeanor conviction follows 411.073 instead).
nuggets.quote: A court may not issue an order of nondisclosure of criminal history record information under this section if the court determines that the offense for which the order is sought, other than an offense under Section 22.01, Penal Code, was violent or sexual in nature. (d) A person may petition the court that imposed the sentence for an order of nondisclosure of criminal history record information under this section only on or after: (1) the date of completion of the person's sentence, if the offense of which the person was convicted was a misdemeanor punishable by fine only; or (2) the second anniversary of the date of completion of the person's sentence, if the offense of which the person was convicted was a misdemeanor other than a misdemeanor described by Subdivision (1)

answer:
Expunction erases arrest records. A trial acquittal qualifies [N1]. Otherwise the case must not have ended in conviction, be pending, or led to court-ordered supervision like deferred adjudication (Class C excepted) [N2], and you need a ground: no charge filed and 180 days (Class C), one year (Class A/B) or three years (felony or related felony charge) since arrest, or the prosecutor's certification [N3]; dismissal for a listed reason, like completing a veterans, mental health or pretrial program, or no probable cause [N4]; or expired limitations [N5]. File in the district court of the county of arrest or offense [N6]. Cost: the civil filing fee (base $137 state, $213 local) [N8][N9] plus other fees [N7], or $100 in a justice or municipal court of record for fine-only offenses [N7].

After deferred adjudication, ask the court that placed you on it for an order of nondisclosure, hiding the record from the public: at discharge for most non-DWI misdemeanors, two years after for assault, sex, weapons and similar misdemeanors, five years for felonies [N10]. For many first-time misdemeanors the court must issue it for $28, at discharge or after 180 days [N14]. First-time misdemeanor convictions other than DWI qualify, unless violent or sexual (simple assault aside), when a fine-only sentence ends, otherwise two years after a jail sentence [N15]. A new offense other than fine-only traffic during supervision or the wait [N11], or any sex-offender, murder, trafficking, stalking or family-violence offense, ever [N12], bars it. Petitions cost the civil filing fee [N13][N8][N9].

gaps: The process shows two alternative tracks. Expunction (Code of Criminal Procedure Chapter 55A) is for arrests that did not end in a final conviction or court-ordered community supervision (other than Class C), acquittals, and pardons; an order of nondisclosure (Government Code Chapter 411, Subchapter E-1) seals the record of a completed deferred adjudication or of certain completed sentences from the public. The waiting periods (55A.052(a)(1)-(3); 411.0725(e), 411.0735(d), 411.073(d), 411.0726(f), 411.0731(f), 411.0736(f)) are preconditions to filing, not deadlines, and are encoded in the decision tables rather than as timers.

The 30-day period in 55A.254(a) is a minimum before the hearing, not a deadline. The petition must be verified and list every agency and private entity believed to hold records (55A.253); the clerk charges $25 for each listed entity that cannot receive electronic notice (55A.254(f)) and again for the order (55A.351(b-3)).

Fast tracks not drawn: after a trial acquittal the order is entered within 30 days on request and the filing fee is waived if the petition is filed within 30 days (55A.201, 102.0061(c)); actual-innocence pardons (55A.202) and veterans or mental health court dismissals (55A.203, no fee) are handled by the trial court; mistaken-identity expunction goes through the felony prosecutor and the court rules without a hearing (55A.256); fine-only arrests may be filed in a justice court or municipal court of record for $100 (55A.252, 102.0061(b)).

Automatic nondisclosure (411.072): for a first-time deferred adjudication on a misdemeanor outside the excluded chapters, the court must issue the order on discharge if 180 days have passed since the deferral (or as soon as practicable after the 180th day), on payment of $28; no petition is filed.

The nondisclosure decision table simplifies several sections that share one pattern (411.0725, 411.0726, 411.073, 411.0731, 411.0735, 411.0736): each requires eligibility, notice to the state, an opportunity for a hearing, and a finding that the order is in the best interest of justice. DWI-related petitions also fail if the prosecutor shows the offense caused a collision involving another person; misdemeanor convictions that were violent or sexual (other than Penal Code 22.01 assault) are excluded (411.0735(c-1)).

A hearing is required before a nondisclosure order unless the state does not request one before the 45th day after notice and the court finds the person entitled and the order in the best interest of justice (411.0745(e)); the missed 45-day request is drawn as the path straight to the decision.

The agency deadlines after a nondisclosure order (15, 10 and 30 business days, 411.075) state no consequence for missing them; the generated 'Deadline missed' ends are not statutory outcomes. The clerk also seals the court's own records (411.076(b)). After expunction the clerk keeps the file closed and destroys it after one year in most cases (55A.356); expunction may let agencies keep records for a pending investigation (55A.302).
The final steps of expunction depend on the order becoming final (55A.351(a)); either the person or a protesting agency may appeal (55A.303).

The expunction decision table models only acquittal (55A.002) and the Subchapter B grounds (55A.052-55A.054); its last rule means 'not entitled on these grounds', not 'not entitled at all'. Other routes exist: pardon, including for actual innocence (55A.003, 55A.004), a pre-September 1, 2021 unlawful-carrying-of-handgun conviction (55A.005), mistaken identity (55A.006, 55A.256), and the court's discretionary expunction after an appellate acquittal or on the prosecutor's recommendation before trial (55A.101). A person who intentionally or knowingly absconds after release loses the waiting-period and limitations grounds (55A.154); that bar is folded into the input labels rather than drawn as a separate rule.

Missing the 45-day request window (411.0745(e)(1)) is modeled as 'right-lapses' because the state can no longer force a hearing; the court may still hold one, and it may decide without a hearing only if it also finds the person entitled to file and the order in the best interest of justice (411.0745(e)(2)).

version_flags: Expunction is codified in Code of Criminal Procedure Chapter 55A (Articles 55A.001-55A.451), the nonsubstantive recodification of former Chapter 55; older guides, forms and court opinions cite the former articles (for example 55.01 for eligibility, 55.02 for procedure and 55.03 for the effect of an order).
Article 55A.356(d) and (e) were repealed by Acts 2025, 89th Leg., R.S., Ch. 850 (S.B. 1667), eff. September 1, 2025, as noted in the downloaded text.
No section relied on carries an '(Effective ...)' or '(Effective until ...)' heading in the downloaded text as of 2026-10-10.
local_option: The district clerk keeps the county's list of agencies and e-mail addresses for expunction petitions (55A.253(c)); the total civil filing fee differs by county; the prosecutor decides whether to certify that records are not needed (55A.052(a)(4)) and whether to request a hearing on a nondisclosure petition (411.0745(e)).
notes: Texas has no general 'sealing' statute for adult records: expunction (Code Crim. Proc. ch. 55A) destroys or returns arrest records and lets the person deny the arrest (55A.401), while an order of nondisclosure (Gov't Code ch. 411, subch. E-1) bars criminal justice agencies and courts from disclosing the record to the public but leaves it available to criminal justice agencies, licensing bodies and the entities listed in 411.0765, and admissible in a later prosecution (411.0775); the person need not disclose it on job, information or licensing applications (411.0755). Expunction routes: acquittal (55A.002; 55A.201 order within 30 days on request), pardon (55A.003-.004), pre-September 1, 2021 handgun carrying conviction (55A.005), mistaken identity (55A.006, 55A.256), no charge presented after 180 days / one year / three years or with the prosecutor's certification (55A.052), dismissal for listed reasons (55A.053), expired limitations (55A.054), appellate acquittal or the prosecutor's recommendation (55A.101); exclusions: same-episode conviction (55A.151), driver's license suspensions (55A.152), community supervision revocation warrants (55A.153), absconding (55A.154). Cost detail: 102.0061(a) ties the district-court fee to the ordinary civil ex parte filing fee, which in the code is built from the $137 state consolidated civil fee (Local Gov't Code 133.151(a)(1)) and the $213 local consolidated civil fee (Local Gov't Code 135.101(a)(1)) plus any county-specific fees (the same two fees apply in statutory county and county courts, so a nondisclosure petition under 411.0745(b) has the same $350 base); $25 per entity without electronic delivery (55A.254(f), 55A.351(b-3)); waivers for acquittal petitions filed within 30 days and veterans or mental health court completions (102.0061(c)-(d)); the court may refund the district-court fee when it grants the petition (102.0061(e)). Nondisclosure: deferred adjudication waiting periods in 411.0725(e) (at discharge, second anniversary for Penal Code chapters 20, 21, 22, 25, 42, 43, 46, fifth anniversary for felonies); DWI deferred (411.0726, second anniversary), DWI probation (411.0731, two or five years), DWI conviction (411.0736, three or five years, depending on six months of ignition interlock); misdemeanor probation after conviction (411.073: first offenders only; at completion of the community supervision for most misdemeanors, second anniversary for Penal Code chapters 20, 21, 22, 25, 42, 43, 46); misdemeanor conviction with a completed sentence (411.0735: first offenders only, not for persons eligible under 411.073; at completion if fine-only, otherwise second anniversary; not violent or sexual except Penal Code 22.01 assault); veterans treatment court (411.0727) and trafficking victims (411.0728) have their own routes; felony convictions are otherwise not covered. Every order requires 411.074: no new non-traffic offense during supervision or the waiting period, and no excluded offense. The court must tell a defendant of the nondisclosure right before deferred adjudication (42A.106(b)), and the releasing officer must explain expunction rights on release (55A.451). Juvenile records follow a separate sealing scheme in Family Code ch. 58, subch. C-1 (automatic sealing at 19 for non-felony delinquent conduct, 58.253; application to the juvenile court with no filing fee, 58.256), and minors' fine-only convictions have their own expunction in Code Crim. Proc. 45A.463 ($30 reimbursement fee).
